parameters.text:
=You are a summarisation agent.
Your job is to summarise each document provided in this batch, independently and in depth.

## Input Structure
You will receive a batch containing multiple files:
- batch_index: {{ $json.batch_index }} of {{ $json.total_batches }}
- file_count: {{ $json.file_count }} files in this batch

## Instructions
Summarise EACH file separately. Do not merge or cross-reference files.

For each file, produce one summary block using this structure:

## {fileName}
{summary}



## Summary Depth Guide
Scale based on estimated_tokens of each file:

* Small (< 2000 tokens)
- 2–3 solid paragraphs
- Cover the main topic, key points, and any conclusions

* Medium (2000–30000 tokens)
- Overview paragraph
- Detailed bullet points covering ALL major sections and topics
- Key findings, arguments, or conclusions
- Any important data, figures, or outcomes mentioned

* Large (> 30000 tokens)
- Overview paragraph (what the document is, its purpose)
- Comprehensive section-by-section breakdown
- Key findings and supporting detail for each
- Important data, figures, methodologies mentioned
- Conclusions and implications

## Rules
- Be thorough, a summary should give the reader a genuinely useful understanding of the document without reading it
- Never fabricate content not present in the document
- Never refer to "batch", "tokens", or technical metadata in your output
- Write naturally as if summarising standalone documents
- If a fileName contains "(part X/Y)", note briefly that this is a section of a larger document
- If content appears cut off or incomplete, mention it at the end of that file's summary
- Separate each file summary with a markdown divider:
- Do NOT produce one-line or one-paragraph summaries for medium or large documents

## Files to Summarise
{{ $json.files.map((f, i) => `### File ${i+1}: ${f.fileName} (~${f.estimated_tokens} tokens)\n\n${f.content}`).join('\n\n---\n\n') }}

parameters.content:
## User chat to interact with the system.

#### - The system mainly for attaching files and requiring a task.
#### - The user can attach files including pdf, txt, docx, csv, xls, and xlsx.
#### - If the user asked something without attaching a file, the Chat agent will instruct the user the best way.

## Tasks the system can preform:
#### - Summarisation
#### - Classification
#### - Data Extraction

## Summariser Agent

#### This is a specialised agent in summarisation, summarise each file independently, or splitting the large files into smaller chunks
#### with overlaps making the summarisation more accurate.

#### The agent summarise the files in points to give the user a good overview for each file.

## Orchestrator Agent

#### The orchestrator analyse the user message and decides which specialised agent to call.

#### There are 3 specialised agents:
##### - Summariser
##### - Classifier
##### - Data Extractor

##### Otherwise, the orchestrator rejects the user's request and instruct the user about the existing tasks.

## Data Extractor Agent

#### The data extraction agent, extracts from each file the key information, including:
##### - Key parties (e.g. names, companies, shipping company)
##### - Key numbers (e.g account number, order number)
##### - Key dates (e.g. issue date, due date)
##### - Main addresses (e.g. shipping address, return address, home address)
##### - Billing breakdown (e.g. total amount, tax, unit price)
##### - Item information (eg. item name, quantity, price)
##### - Payment (e.g. amount paid, payment method)

## Classifier Agent

#### The agent classifies each file independently, giving an output of:
##### - File name
##### - File type
##### - File category
##### - One line of an overview of the file
